titulo_es: Future forms compared (will, going to, present continuous and present simple)
descripcion_es: When to use will, be going to, the present continuous and the present simple to talk about the future.
resumen: English has several future forms, and the choice depends on whether it is a spontaneous decision, a plan, a fixed arrangement, a prediction or a timetable.

filas: Decision at the moment of speaking, offer, promise, prediction based on opinion
It's cold. I'll close the window.
I'm going to study law next year.
Prediction based on what you can see now
Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
Fixed arrangement (date, time, with other people)

items: With think, probably, perhaps, I'm sure, will is usually used: I think Spain will win.
After when, as soon as, before, after, until, if, use the present, not will: I'll call you when I arrive.
Shall I / Shall we? to offer or suggest: Shall I help you?
Won't = will not; it also expresses refusal to do something: The car won't start.

explicacion.texto: The difference between going to and the present continuous is small: the continuous implies that it is already organised (ticket, booking, arrangement to meet). I'm going to see a doctor (I have decided); I'm seeing the doctor at 10 (I have an appointment).

ejemplos.frase: The phone is ringing. — I'll get it!
ejemplos.traduccion: Está sonando el teléfono. — ¡Ya lo cojo yo!

ejemplos.frase: We're going to paint the kitchen this weekend.
ejemplos.traduccion: Vamos a pintar la cocina este fin de semana.

ejemplos.frase: She's flying to Mexico on Friday.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se va en avión a México el viernes.

ejemplos.frase: The museum opens at ten tomorrow.
ejemplos.traduccion: El museo abre mañana a las diez.

ejemplos.frase: Careful! You're going to drop those glasses.
ejemplos.traduccion: ¡Cuidado! Se te van a caer esos vasos.

ejemplos.frase: I'll text you as soon as I get home.
ejemplos.traduccion: Te escribo en cuanto llegue a casa.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I will call you when I will arrive.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I will call you when I arrive.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After when, as soon as, before, until… use the present, just like the Spanish subjunctive “cuando llegue”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I go to the dentist tomorrow at five.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I'm going to the dentist tomorrow at five.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A fixed personal arrangement goes in the present continuous, not the present simple (which is kept for timetables).

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Do you want a coffee? — Yes, I'm going to have one.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Do you want a coffee? — Yes, I'll have one.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A decision made at the moment of speaking is expressed with will.

ejercicios.frase: This bag looks heavy. — Don't worry, I ___ carry it for you.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: will + infinitive for decisions made at the moment of speaking and for offers. The clue is the immediate reaction to what the other person has just said (This bag looks heavy) and the phrase Don't worry: the decision to help is made at that instant. That is why the form is will: I'll carry it for you. Spanish would use the present (“te la llevo”), which may lead you to choose another form.
ejercicios.traduccion: Esta bolsa parece pesada. — No te preocupes, yo te la llevo.

por_opcion.will: Correct: an offer decided at the moment of speaking.
por_opcion.am going to: Incorrect: going to indicates a previous intention, and here the decision is made at that instant.
por_opcion.am carrying: Incorrect: the present continuous for the future expresses an arrangement or organised plan, not a spontaneous offer.

ejercicios.frase: We've bought the tickets. We ___ to Rome in May.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table and in the final text of the card: the present continuous expresses an arranged plan that is already organised (ticket, booking, arrangement to meet). The clue is We've bought the tickets: the trip is not just an intention, it is organised. That is why the form is are going (present continuous of go). Going to go would also be possible in real usage, but it is not among the options.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ya hemos comprado los billetes. Vamos a Roma en mayo.

por_opcion.will go: Incorrect: will would present the trip as a decision made on the spot or a prediction, not as a plan already organised.
por_opcion.are going: Correct: present continuous for an organised plan (tickets bought).
por_opcion.go: Incorrect: the present simple is kept for timetables and fixed schedules, not for personal plans.

ejercicios.frase: The concert ___ at 9 p.m., according to the programme.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: the present simple for timetables and fixed schedules. The clue is according to the programme, which shows that the time does not depend on anyone's intention but on a published programme. That is why the form is starts, in the present simple with the third-person -s, just like The train leaves at 8.15.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Fixed time in a programme: present simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: El concierto empieza a las 9 de la noche, según el programa.

por_opcion.starts: Correct: a fixed time in a programme, present simple.
por_opcion.is going to start: Incorrect: going to expresses intention or a prediction based on evidence, not an official timetable.
por_opcion.will be starting: Incorrect: the future continuous is not the natural form for a fixed programme.

ejercicios.frase: Look at that man on the ladder! He ___ fall.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: be going to for a prediction based on what you can see now. The clue is Look at…!: the speaker sees something at that moment that allows them to anticipate the fall. That is why the form is is going to fall, just like the example on the card Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Prediction based on what you can see: going to.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¡Mira a ese hombre en la escalera! Se va a caer.

por_opcion.will: Incorrect: will is used for predictions based on opinion; with visible evidence in front of you, the card requires going to.
por_opcion.is going to: Correct: a prediction based on present evidence.
por_opcion.falls: Incorrect: the present simple for the future is for timetables, not for predictions.

glosario.definicion_l: steps consisting of two parallel members connected by rungs; for climbing up or down · ascending stages by which somebody or something can progress

ejercicios.frase: I'll wait here until you ___ back.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the point in Rules and key points: after when, as soon as, before, after, until and if, use the present, not will. The clue is until, which introduces a time clause about the future. That is why the form is come, in the present simple. Spanish does something similar with the subjunctive (“hasta que vuelvas”), not with the future.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After until, use the present simple.

por_opcion.will come: Incorrect: will is not used after until, even if the action is in the future.
por_opcion.come: Correct: present simple in the time clause introduced by until.
por_opcion.are going to come: Incorrect: going to is not used in the time clause either; the present is enough.

ejercicios.frase: I promise I ___ tell anyone your secret.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: will for promises, and won't = will not as the negative form. The clue is I promise, which calls for will, and the meaning of the sentence: the promise is not to tell. That is why the answer is won't (or the full form will not, more emphatic or written).
ejercicios.traduccion: Te prometo que no le contaré a nadie tu secreto.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With will the sentence would promise to tell everyone; you need the negative won't.
Don't is the present negative; for a promise about the future, use won't.
The apostrophe is missing: the contraction of will not is won't.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the going to form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: My sister ___ (start) a new job next month. She decided last week.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: be going to + infinitive for an intention or a plan already decided. The clue is She decided last week: the decision was made before the moment of speaking. The form agrees with my sister (third person singular): is going to start, or contracted 's going to start.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Intention already decided: be going to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi hermana va a empezar un trabajo nuevo el mes que viene. Lo decidió la semana pasada.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Will expresses a decision made on the spot; here the decision has already been made and the exercise asks for going to.
It does not agree: my sister is third person singular, so is.
After going to comes the infinitive, not -ing.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the present simple or with will.
ejercicios.frase: As soon as the results ___ (be) ready, we'll publish them.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the point in Rules and key points: after as soon as, use the present, not will. The clue is As soon as at the beginning of the time clause; the future is already in the main clause (we'll publish). The subject the results is plural, so the present of be is are. Spanish uses the subjunctive “estén”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After as soon as, use the present, not will.
ejercicios.traduccion: En cuanto estén listos los resultados, los publicaremos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Will is not used after as soon as, even if the action is in the future.
The present is correct, but the results is plural: are.
It is a literal copy of the Spanish subjunctive “estén”; English uses the present indicative are.

ejercicios.frase: ___ we take a taxi? It's getting late.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the point in Rules and key points: Shall I / Shall we? to offer or suggest. The clue is the subject we and the intention of proposing something to the other person, justified by It's getting late. That is why the answer is Shall. Will we take a taxi? would be a question about what is going to happen, not a suggestion.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Suggestion with the first person: Shall we…?
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Cogemos un taxi? Se está haciendo tarde.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Will we…? asks about a future fact; to make a suggestion with the first person, use Shall we…?
Do we take a taxi? asks about a habit or a plan; it does not make a suggestion.
Let's is used to propose something, but it does not form a question with we after it.

ejercicios.frase: If it will rain, we'll stay at home.
respuestas: If it rains, we'll stay at home.
If it rains, we will stay at home.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the point in Rules and key points: after if, use the present, not will. The clue is the conjunction If and the future already present in the main clause (we'll stay). The correction is If it rains: present simple with the third-person -s. Both we'll and we will are accepted in the main clause.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In the if clause, use the present simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si llueve, nos quedaremos en casa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If it will rain, we'll stay at home.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: after if comes the present, not will.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If it rain, we'll stay at home.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It uses the present but forgets the third-person -s: rains.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If it rains, we stay at home.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It removes will from the main clause; the future consequence needs will.

ejercicios.frase: I think Real Madrid wins the league next season.
respuestas: I think Real Madrid will win the league next season.
I think Real Madrid is going to win the league next season.
I think Real Madrid are going to win the league next season.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the point in Rules and key points: with I think, probably, perhaps or I'm sure, will is usually used for a prediction based on opinion. The clue is I think and next season, a future prediction. The present simple wins does not work, because it is not a timetable. Going to is also accepted, and with a team the verb can be singular or plural (is/are going to), as is usual in British English.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Prediction based on opinion with I think: will.
ejercicios.traduccion: Creo que el Real Madrid ganará la liga la próxima temporada.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I think Real Madrid wins the league next season.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: a prediction based on opinion does not go in the present simple.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I think Real Madrid will wins the league next season.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After will comes the infinitive without -s: will win.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I think Real Madrid is winning the league next season.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present continuous for the future is for organised arrangements, not for predictions.

ejercicios.frase: Shall you help me with this box?
respuestas: Will you help me with this box?
Can you help me with this box?
Could you help me with this box?
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the point in Rules and key points: shall is used with I and we to offer or suggest. The clue is the subject you: nothing is being offered; a favour is being asked of another person. To ask for something you use Will you…?, Can you…? or Could you…? (the last one is the most polite), so all three are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To ask another person for something, use Will/Can/Could you, not Shall you.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Shall you help me with this box?
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: shall is not used with you to ask for something.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Do you help me with this box?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Do you…? asks about a habit; to ask a favour, use Will/Can/Could you.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Shall I help me with this box?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Shall I offers help to the other person; with me the sentence makes no sense.

respuestas: I'm meeting Tom at eight tonight
I'm meeting Tom tonight at eight
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: the present continuous for an appointment or a plan arranged with a date, a time and other people. The clue is the arrangement with Tom at a specific time, at eight tonight. The order is subject + verb (I'm meeting) + object (Tom) + time expressions; the two time expressions can go in either order, so two solutions are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: He quedado con Tom esta noche a las ocho.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm meeting at eight tonight Tom
errores_previstos.explicacion: In English the object goes right next to the verb; time expressions go after it: meeting Tom at eight tonight.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tonight I'm at eight meeting Tom
errores_previstos.explicacion: It separates the verb from its auxiliary with another element; the natural order is I'm meeting Tom…

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: be going to + infinitive for a prediction based on what you can see now, as in the example on the card It's going to rain. The order is subject with be (it's) + going to + infinitive (rain). There are no extra elements: the structure is fixed.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Prediction with evidence: be going to + infinitive.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It changes the fixed structure: going to + infinitive, not to going.
The subject with be goes first: it's going to rain.

descripcion_larga_es: English does not have a single future: it chooses between will, be going to, the present continuous and the present simple depending on whether it is a spontaneous decision, a plan, a fixed arrangement, a prediction or a timetable. Mastering this choice is essential for talking about plans and forecasts naturally. Spanish speakers find it difficult because in Spanish the simple future or “ir a” work for almost everything.

contexto.que_es: It is the comparison of the four main ways of talking about the future: will + infinitive, be going to + infinitive, the present continuous and the present simple. Each one expresses a different relationship between the speaker and the future event: a decision at the moment of speaking, a previous intention, an arranged appointment, a prediction or a fixed schedule.
contexto.por_que_importa: Talking about plans, forecasts and commitments is constant in any conversation or professional text. Choosing wrongly does not usually prevent understanding, but it changes the nuance: I'm going to have one when you decide on the spot sounds odd, and I go to the dentist tomorrow sounds like a timetable rather than an appointment. In addition, will after when or if is one of the most heavily penalised mistakes in exams.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: The signals are clear: offers and promises (will), I think or probably (will), visible evidence (going to), tickets bought or appointments with a time (present continuous), programmes and timetables (present simple). After when, as soon as, until, before and if, use the present, like the Spanish subjunctive “cuando llegue”. Spanish speakers tend to put will everywhere, including where Spanish would use the subjunctive.
